A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CASA research, with shared backbones, datasets, experiments, and retained results despite substantial reframing. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Helium-based training, Qwen2.5-VL adaptation, ablations, efficiency measurements, and video-captioning experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original cross-attention training and adaptation results, architectural comparisons, video evaluations, efficiency measurements, and training curves, alongside retained original results.

M1.justification: The original parallel CASA operation survives as CAt+v; that renaming alone is not a method change. However, v2 introduces shared CA/self-attention projections and replacement of self-attention layers with plain CA. Video-QA processing also changes from a whole-video attention window to per-frame windows using image delimiters to retain compressed history, with the all-frame alternative additionally evaluated.

E1.justification: The represented dataset and task coverage remains image understanding, video QA, and live captioning, using the same FineVision, LLaVA-OneVision, LLaVA-Video, and Live-Whisper dataset families. The nine image benchmarks, five video benchmarks, and LiveSports3K evaluation are retained. Windowing, resolution, and architectural comparisons change procedures within this coverage.

E2.justification: The external baseline set in Table 2 is retained. However, v2 Figure 1 adds EVLM-Chat 14B and StreamChat to its image comparison, and Table 4 adds StreamChat to video comparisons. The controlled gated/register cross-attention comparisons and the Q-64 qualitative caption comparison from v1 are removed.

E3.justification: Helium training changes from 100k to 40k steps, and Qwen image adaptation from 60k in v1's main text or 65k in its appendix to 25k. Training resolution changes from 896 squared pixels for CASA and 672 squared for insertion to 952 squared for both; video resolution changes from 448 squared to 504 squared. V2 increases insertion gradient accumulation to match token budgets and introduces explicit per-frame versus all-frame video comparisons and revised efficiency measurements.

E4.justification: V1's self-versus-random-token masking experiment, attention-distribution analysis, and detailed layer-placement study are removed or replaced. V2 adds parameter-sharing and revised layer-frequency comparisons, contrasts video-history mechanisms, and expands convergence analysis to individual benchmarks for both backbones. FFN-update and token-compression analyses remain, while the detailed layer-level profiling and Q-64 qualitative case study disappear.

E5.justification: V1 Table 11 explicitly averages profiling measurements across 100 calls. That experiment and its repetition-count disclosure are absent from v2, whose replacement efficiency table gives no equivalent count. Neither version reports seed-based accuracy uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The main image and video result tables contain substantially replaced and added results. For example, the parallel joint-attention Helium model's ChartQA score changes from 73.8 to 75.3 under revised training conditions, so this is not an established same-setting gain. The Q-Former-128 aggregate changes from 62.7 to 63.8 despite unchanged component scores. Conversely, the FFN-update ablation and LiveSports captioning scores are retained.

T1.justification: The attention equations largely match after renaming, including v1 Equation 3 and v2 Equation 4. Formal efficiency content changes: v1's theoretical attention-memory expressions in Table 1 and Figure 3 are replaced by per-variant KV-cache counts in v2 Table 1. Neither version contains substantive theorem or proof developments.

C1.justification: V1 presents CASA as a new fusion mechanism whose local text self-attention and implicit gating are crucial to closing the performance gap. V2 instead centers the claim that vanilla cross-attention is competitive under comparable modern training, with joint text-image attention becoming one variant. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace the original novelty claim with a controlled comparison organized around five design differences.

C2.justification: V1's explanation that missing text interaction causes cross-attention's weakness, and that implicit gating remedies it, is withdrawn. V2 emphasizes training comparability and interprets joint text-image attention as offering little average advantage over vanilla CA. It also develops the limitations of losing explicit visual history, the proposed role of delimiter tokens as compressed memory, and the tradeoffs of parameter sharing and layer replacement.

D1.justification: The reproducibility recipe is substantially revised: v2 documents different accumulation settings, training horizons and runtimes, and reports AdamW instead of Adam. It specifies frame-wise video windows, delimiter-based history, absence of positional embeddings in plain CA, and frozen image temporal positions for CAt+v. V1's detailed profiler procedure and explicit caption-training mixture description are removed. The project-page access and code/model-release statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The relationship to prior work changes from proposing a necessary architectural remedy for existing cross-attention approaches to arguing that standard cross-attention was underestimated under differing training pipelines. V2 adds gist-token/context-compression positioning and citations such as LXMERT and linear-transformer work, while removing several positional/context-extension references. This is a substantive repositioning, beyond citation renumbering.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method narrative, experimental discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The CASA-centered approach section becomes a five-part comparison of cross-attention and token insertion, terminology changes throughout, and the appendices are reorganized after removing the implicit-gating section.

P2.justification: The opening radar comparison becomes a normalized grouped bar chart, and the architecture/attention illustrations are reorganized into a combined multipanel figure. Efficiency and video tables receive substantially different structures; the captioning score table is combined with a redrawn latency plot. The memory-growth and attention-distribution figures disappear, while two detailed benchmark-wise training-curve figures replace the earlier grouped curve.

improvement.justification: V2 resolves an important comparison confound: v1 Table 2 uses 0.3T training tokens for CASA versus 0.1T for insertion, with different training resolutions; v2 uses 0.13T and the same maximum resolution for both. The resulting controlled comparisons support a more measured conclusion about vanilla cross-attention and are complemented by explicit video-history controls. Some profiling detail is lost, and appendix inconsistencies remain, including old resolution values in Section B.2, but the improved validity of the central comparison constitutes a substantial overall gain.
